📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since George Lazenby first replaced Sean Connery as James Bond in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service,” fans have argued over who makes the best 007 — and those arguments are likely to resume once Robert Pattinson takes the screen as the latest Bond in director Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming iteration. Although Craig has his partisans, Connery tends to be the consensus choice for the best Bond, though I’ve argued here for the merits of 1970s and ’80s Roger Moore. All the Bonds have their virtues, but Connery benefited from being there first — for anyone who discovered the series in its initial heyday, Connery simply is James Bond. Related Stories ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Christmas Special Trailer: Can Mary Bennet Still Be Herself and ‘the Perfect Wife’? ‘Madden’ Review: David O. Russell Fumbles Again with an Unfunny and Purposeless Football Biopic.

Yet Connery actually wasn’t the first actor to play Bond. That honor goes to journeyman MGM contract player Barry Nelson, who played Bond in a “Casino Royale” adaptation eight years before Connery made the character famous in “Dr. No.” Connery may have been the first 007 to grace the significant screen, but Nelson established Bond on the small screen in an episode of the CBS anthology series “Climax!” opposite Peter Lorre in the Le Chiffre role that would later be inhabited by Orson Welles (in the goofy 1967 “Casino Royale”) and Mads Mikkelsen (in the 2006 adaptation that introduced Craig to the series).

Recent findings suggest that the 1954 “Casino Royale” is a fascinating artifact that includes elements that would go on to characterize future James Bond movies, while also going in a few other very different directions. The key difference is in the scale, stripped down by necessity for television production. The hour-long “Climax!” episode is all interiors, taking place entirely in the hotel and casino of the title. It’s more a James Bond play than a movie, with Bond and Le Chiffre facing off in a series of verbal — and ultimately physical — jousts in confined spaces, and it’s surprisingly effective.

Industry observers note that it’s also a very strange beginning for a franchise that would come to be known for its globetrotting locales and elaborate action set pieces. Not that this “Casino Royale” was officially part of the James Bond franchise as we know it. In fact, although there have been three adaptations of Ian Fleming’s first James Bond novel, only the third incarnation with Daniel Craig was from EON Productions, the manufacturer that controlled the character from “Dr. No” through the Craig era before selling the rights to Amazon.

Sources indicate that the 1954 “Casino Royale” came about when producer Gregory Ratoff optioned the rights to Fleming’s novel in May of that year. The novel wasn’t yet a hit, and Fleming was sorely in need of cash, which led him to make one of the worst deals in movie-rights history when he sold the book outright to Ratoff for $6,000 after the TV episode aired. This left “Casino Royale” out of the deal when EON secured the screen rights to James Bond as a character, so Bond producers Albert Broccoli and Harry Saltzman could only sit back and grit their teeth when Ratoff turned “Casino Royale” into a comedy in 1967 and cast Peter Sellers, David Niven, Woody Allen and others as rotating Bonds.

According to recent reports, EON ultimately made a deal to bring “Casino Royale” under their umbrella and used the novel to reboot the franchise with Craig, but in 1954 it served as the source for a much more modest affair. The biggest similarities between the 1954 “Climax!” episode and the Daniel Craig movie come in the time spent on extended gambling sequences, and the centering of a brutal torture scene. Given censorship restrictions of the time, Nelson’s torture in a bathtub is considerably less graphic than the mallet to the testicles inflicted on Craig, but it’s rough enough stuff for a 1950s TV production.

It has been revealed that certain aspects of Nelson’s characterization, like Bond’s mix of sexual swagger and icy indifference, would later be adopted by most future 007s, to varying degrees. The biggest difference between Nelson and future Bonds is a simple one: He’s American. Although Broccoli and Saltzman flirted with the idea of an American Bond throughout the series’ history (going so far as to cast James Brolin in “Octopussy” before Moore decided to return at the last minute), to date they’ve never actually pulled the trigger on casting outside the UK.

Nelson is probably best known to modern audiences as the affable hotel manager Stuart Ullman in Stanley Kubrick’s “The Shining,” but in the 1950s he was a sturdy character actor and occasional leading man who bounced around television after an initial sojourn as a studio contract player. As a young man, he appeared in several important MGM films, including “Shadow of the Thin Man,” “Bataan,” and “A Guy Named Joe” (the source material for Steven Spielberg’s “Always”). Later on, he popped up in “Airport” and had a successful Broadway career. He was nominated for a Tony acting opposite Liza Minnelli in Martin Scorsese’s 1977 production “The Act.”.

In 1954, though, he was in the middle of a prolific and productive era as a TV stalwart, both as a series regular (on “The Hunter” and “My Favorite Husband”) and a frequent guest star. He doesn’t exhibit a ton of range as American “Combined Intelligence” agent “Jimmy” Bond, but that too is in keeping with the overall conception of the character, at least until Craig tried to bring a little more emotional depth to the role.

Sources indicate that in Americanizing Bond, the “Climax!” edition of “Casino Royale” ends up making a number of related changes that are small but make the film feel just a bit off for fans of the EON productions. American Felix Leiter (later played by Jeffrey Wright) becomes Brit Clarence Leiter, for example. Although there’s none of the Bond gadgetry that would become famous later, there are hints of what’s to come in the form of props like a villain’s cane that hides a gun, and the opening credits for the “Climax!” series itself feature a gun barrel pointed at the viewer that predicts the iconic graphics of later Bond title sequences.

The 1954 “Casino Royale” is noteworthy for another reason: its composer, Jerry Goldsmith, who would ultimately score hundreds of major films, including “Planet of the Apes,” “Chinatown,” “Basic Instinct,” and most of Joe Dante’s work. Yet in some ways what’s fascinating about “Casino Royale” is how unremarkable it is — it’s a decent, solid piece of entertainment from an era when proliferating anthology reveals provided similar programs every week.

If Fleming had his way, it would have only been the start for 007 on television; he wrote several outlines for episodes of a James Bond series before CBS canceled the project. Luckily, he repurposed most of what he wrote as short stories for his 1960 book “For Your Eyes Only,” and television’s loss was cinema’s gain. By 1962, James Bond belonged to the movies — and to Sean Connery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blade Runner, Ridley Scott’s 1982 adaptation of Philip K. Dick’s 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, is one of the best and most influential sci-fi films of all time, but it took 35 years for it to get a direct sequel. Producers Broderick Johnson and Andrew Kosove acquired the rights to the franchise in 2011 through their production company, Alcon, and used them to develop Denis Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049, which is set 30 years after the events of Scott’s film. Now, the timeline is moving forward again in Blade Runner 2099, which premieres on Prime Video on Nov. 25, and the producers are already thinking about what’s next for the cyberpunk series after that.

“We've been very judicious not to overexpose the IP or flood the marketplace, but strategically we're always thinking about the next chapters in the franchise,” Johnson tells Polygon. “This was a long, challenging, but very fulfilling journey that we hope audiences enjoy that really fills out a lot more of the mythology because it's all in canon. We're definitely thinking about latest things to do with the next iteration.”.

It has been revealed that blade Runner 2099 has been in development since 2021, and was disrupted by the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike and the departure of director and executive producer Jeremy Podeswa. Johnson claims managing such a beloved property is “a blessing and a challenge.” Annapurna Interactive confirmed in 2023 that it was working on a video game adaptation titled Blade Runner 2023: Labyrinth, but that project seems to have been scrapped after most of the team resigned in 2024. The producers have also spoken with game studios about making a AAA game in the style of Cyberpunk 2077.

Recent findings suggest that “People approach us all the time with different ideas,” Johnson mentioned. “There's a very high bar for anything that you do in this universe. But we love that challenge. It's so dear to artists’ and creators' hearts that we're always getting interesting ideas about what to do next.”.

The Blade Runner franchise also includes a trio of short films and the 2021 animated series Blade Runner: Black Lotus, which are all set between the events of the two movies. Kosove said they’re now trying to decide what storyline they want to explore for their next project, and what the right medium is.

“We may go backwards in the other direction and explore what happened before the first movie,” he claims. “We could continue it in television potentially, and at some point we will certainly go back to film because we believe Blade Runner is fundamentally a theatrical property. But we get inquiries about theater and even opera and other things. We've got a lot of options on our plate and we're exploring them carefully now.”.

In a recent development, in Blade Runner 2099, the Replicants have led a successful uprising against humanity. The series follows the human fugitive Cora (Hunter Schafer) as she teams up with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh), a Replicant with only days left to live, to track down Olwen’s former partner and the secrets he’s hiding. Kosove and Johnson previously worked on The Expanse, and Kosove learned a key lesson from the adaptation of James S.A. Corey’s sci-fi series.

“Ultimately in any genre, you have to care about the characters,” he indicates. “The performances of Hunter and Michelle are amazing. Because it’s television, which is long-form, you can get into character development in a way that’s harder to do in film. We’re really hoping people delve into the characters in a meaningful way.”.

Blade Runner 2099 was written as an 8-episode limited series that wraps up its character arcs, though it leaves plenty of room for expansion.

“As a Blade Runner fan, I would always take more Blade Runner,” showrunner Silka Luisa tells Polygon. “What I love about both films was that they didn’t answer all the questions. You’re not walking out of them knowing exactly what’s going to happen afterwards, and it left space for your own imagination to fill in how it could continue. That’s what we tried to do here.”.

COLLIDER: Charlie, I want to start with you because I think the first episode really has a fun cameo that I don't know how many people are expecting. What was it like to reunite with Charles [Edwards] and get to explore the continuing haunting that Sauron is having with Celebrimbor?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved.
  • In a recent development, once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything.
  • Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. It also helps to make meals feel filling. Great! But.

In a recent development, once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:.

Take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

According to recent reports, it’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. (I've done the math for various body weights here.) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

Sources indicate that so if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

I think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?

It has been revealed that here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

But then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

It has been revealed that and then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note: The following story contains spoilers for “Paper Tiger.”.

James Gray never hid that Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway were playing fictional versions of his real-life parents in his 2022 drama “Armageddon Time,” based on the writer/director’s experience as a sixth grader growing up in Queens in the 1980s.

“Jeremy is doing my father to such a degree that it is disturbing. He sounds exactly like him, looks exactly like him; it’s bizarre. Annie, too, is uncanny about [playing my mother],” mentioned Gray while a guest on this week’s episode of IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast. “So I had had such a great time with them shooting ‘Armageddon Time,’ I said, ‘Well, why don’t we do this again?’” Related Stories Sean Connery Wasn’t the First James Bond: Meet Barry Nelson in the ‘Casino Royale’ You’ve Never Seen ‘Madden’ Review: David O. Russell Fumbles Again with an Unfunny and Purposeless Football Biopic.

It has been revealed that gray knew his next film (what would become “Paper Tiger”) would be set in 1986 and once again focus on a Jewish family of four, with two sons, in Queens. In the project’s early stages, Hathaway and Strong were up for reprising their roles, but it soon became clear Gray would have to wait 18 months — after both “The Odyssey” (Hathaway) and “The Social Reckoning” (Strong) finished filming — to start production.

Recent findings suggest that “You can’t wait a year and a half,” remarked Gray. “And then I started thinking, ‘Well, maybe this is a blessing in disguise.’ That the [film] could start to take on a fresh style, and so then I started to pursue it in a different way. So in the beginning, in its origin stages, it was [a sequel of sorts], but like any movie, it’s like a wild horse that’s going to get away from you.”.

While Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller’s characters in “Paper Tiger” are inspired by Gray’s parents, they are not as deeply grounded as Hathaway and Strong were in “Armageddon Time” as facsimiles of Gray’s parents in how they talked, looked, dressed, and behaved. Through this lens, Gray began to see the film as less of a straight memoir, freeing him to embrace elements of the crime genre in his storytelling.

Explained Gray, “What I tried to do was to make a film more in — for lack of a better way of really explaining — a bit more Hitchcockian in certain places. Almost — again, ‘pulpy’ is not quite the right word — a little bit more, how do I put this — more of an engagement directly with a tense idea of narrative, that it would be a driving, tense story.”.

What also changed is the sympathetic lens through which Gray now saw his father. In “Paper Tiger,” Irwin (Teller) puts his family in danger when he unwittingly gets entangled (pursuing environmental consulting work for businesses along the polluted Gowanus Canal) with the Russian mob. While Irwin is guilty of pride and naivety, it is (especially compared to Gray’s previous films) a positive portrayal of a hard-working and earnest father pursuing the American dream.

Sources indicate that in this sense, the shift from Strong to Teller was fortuitous. Strong had painted an unforgiving portrait of a miserable, strict father — tortured by generational trauma and unbending with his sons striving for upward mobility — whereas Gray saw something in Teller he could lean into for a different portrayal of his father.

“Miles has a kind of — I can’t believe I’m going to say this, he might even resist this— a softness to him, which would probably offend him, but I think that’s a great thing,” said Gray. “He doesn’t have a softness in his persona. He doesn’t have it in physical terms. It’s actually a tenderness inside. You have to embrace [that] beauty in him and hope it works for the film.”.

When it came to recasting Hathaway, Gray was more practical, saying he needed three characteristics: another bankable star, who was also Jewish, and a real Fresh Yorker. He believed the way the city seeps itself into a person’s bones is not something that even the best actors can learn to portray. Those three unnotiables made Scarlett Johansson the clear number one choice.

Industry observers note that “I had met [Scarlett] years before on a project that never wound up happening, and quite liked her. She’s a total Newly introduced Yorker through and through. Then when I found out that Annie [Hathaway] was going off to do Chris [Nolan’s] movie [‘The Odyssey’] for a thousand years, she was the first choice because you’re talking about one of the biggest stars in the world, and she’s also a Jewish woman from New York,  checks the boxes,” remarked Gray. “When I sent [the script] to her, I sent her a note, ‘There’s probably no chance in hell you’re going to do this, but I love you, can you read this?’ And then she texted me back very, very rapidly and was like, ‘Let’s go.’”.

While Hathaway’s portrayal of Gray’s mother was more open and loving than Strong’s version of his father — and therefore didn’t require as sharp a contrast in how the role was recast — Gray believed Johansson’s approach better fit the needs of “Paper Tiger.”.

“It’s a more operatic idea of character than Annie’s was in ‘Armageddon Time,’” said Gray. “It’s much more a kind of high emotion. And of course, because the situation is much more tragic, and she embraced it completely.”.

“Paper Tiger” opened last weekend in New York and Los Angeles, and expands on November 20.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, from a purely awards-hunting perspective, there’s a great argument to be made that Netflix could have pushed back its late November release “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” until next year. Historically, the perception of the embattled studio is that its had issues being distracted by too big an awards slate to pin down its Best Picture frontrunner. Remember in 2023 when it seemed like the streamer did not realize until the Oscar shortlists (in mid-December!) that “All Quiet on the Western Front” was its best bet at Best Picture? The Edward Berger film went on to win four Oscars, including Best International Feature. Related Stories How ‘Paper Tiger’ Evolved When Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway Couldn’t Reprise Their ‘Armageddon Time’ Roles Sean Connery Wasn’t the First James Bond: Meet Barry Nelson in the ‘Casino Royale’ You’ve Never Seen.

Industry observers note that this year, Netflix is running their best awards campaign yet with “La Bola Negra,” which the studio acquired out of Cannes, where its helmers, Los Javis, won the jury prize for Best Director. Come the fall festivals, it became the first Netflix film to win the People’s Choice Award at TIFF. Since then, it has fronted Netflix’s experiment in expanding the theatrical distribution of its awards slate, doing admirable business in key markets. The consensus among prognosticators is that the film is not only a lock to receive a Best Picture nomination, but is also sure to win the Oscar for Best International Feature on behalf of Spain.

If Netflix wanted to secure a second Best Picture nomination, with “Cliff Booth” out of the picture, the team could put all its energy into Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love.” Not only is the near-three hour film, which won the Grand Jury Prize at Venice, another Best International Feature contender (on behalf of South Korea), but it is one of this season’s most critically lauded films. If enough critics’ groups get behind it in the coming weeks, a la “The Secret Agent” last year, then a second Best Picture nomination for Netflix at the 2027 Oscars becomes highly plausible.

Somewhere along the way, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” became something of a puzzle for Netflix. The streamer had no choice but to follow through with putting it out around Thanksgiving, because it was already set to replace the IMAX screens that had initially been secured for Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia” film. So how does a manufacturer not run an awards campaign for the sequel to a recent Best Picture nominee, directed by a three-time Oscar nominee, written by a two-time Oscar winner, and starring Brad Pitt in the role he just won a Best Supporting Actor Oscar for?

What reads as a home run on paper is more of a double or triple in execution. “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is made by people who know what they are doing, and that expands past director David Fincher, screenwriter Quentin Tarantino, and star Pitt.

Cinematographer Erik Messerschmidt, editor Kirk Baxter, production designer Donald Graham Burt, set decorator Jan Pascale, and composers Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross have all won at least one Academy Award. Costume designer Trish Summerville was nominated for an Oscar for her work on “Mank.” Even if there is a low bar for getting the Academy excited about a late-’70s period piece set in Hollywood, “Cliff Booth” easily clears it.

In a recent development, but we are in a spectacle-heavy year, with “The Odyssey” and “Project Hail Mary” in the awards conversation, and “Dune: Part Three” and “Werwulf” on the horizon. Even “Digger” is a formidable contender in the craft races. So if the feeling is that “Cliff Booth” is more of a hangout movie than a cinematic event, then the focus of its awards campaign should be on categories that are more willing to embrace that, like Best Production Design or Best Costume Design. (Not so much Best Sound, which “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” did actually receive nominations for.).

In terms of the acting performances, again, Pitt is great as Cliff Booth, but there is no rush to nominate him for a performance he already won for. And there are plenty of other Best Actor contenders, like Matt Damon and John Malkovich (who have never won) and John Turturro and Andrew Scott (who have never even been nominated for an Oscar before).

The top performance of the film is with Cliff’s love interest, played by Emmy winner Elizabeth Debicki, who actually does have a shot at her first Oscar nomination, given the love for her performance in “Wicker” as well, and the lack of current consensus in the Best Supporting Actress race.

Everyone else in the film, from Scott Caan to Yahya Abdul-Mateen II to Carla Gugino, is very additive to the project but does not necessarily cross the threshold into Oscar-contender territory. In that way, it is similar to Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!,” another awards hopeful from this season.

Ultimately, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is entertaining enough to garner support from certain branches of the Academy, but falls too late in the year, in too few theaters, to truly become the last-minute surprise blockbuster that would get as many as 10 Oscar nominations, something its predecessor “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” did handily.

Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity.
  • According to recent reports, when you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S.
  • If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

According to recent reports, when you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

Industry observers note that IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

It has been revealed that websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create challenges. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

It has been revealed that webRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

Sources indicate that but the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

In a recent development, even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Recent findings suggest that websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated rapidly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Industry observers note that even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

Industry observers note that while this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

It has been revealed that before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS matter, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:.

Recent findings suggest that we’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Industry observers note that now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Industry observers note that make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

Recent findings suggest that there’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that there’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs.
  • It has been revealed that according to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025.
  • Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

It has been revealed that according to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that customers can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

It has been revealed that the easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Recent findings suggest that reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Sources indicate that look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re presently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

Maybe it’s just because we can’t get enough headlines and discussion about “Backrooms” and “You Can See Everything,” but despite the banner year A24 has had at the box office, its TV division has quietly had nearly as strong of a year.

The indie label has produced more reveals in 2026 than in any year in its history, including sleeper commercial and critical hits across the board, and even managed to land shows on virtually every streamer in town.

Led by Sam French, the U.S. head of TV at A24, the studio this year has cranked out the third season of “Euphoria” on HBO Max, the second season of “Beef” and the third season of “Survival of the Thickest” both on Netflix, “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” on Apple TV, the “Friday the 13th” prequel series “Crystal Lake” on Peacock, and most recently the British sitcom “It Gets Worse” on Paramount+ led by the UK Heads Piers Wenger and Rose Garnett. Its unscripted division, led by Johnny Hausfater, has also ramped up aggressively, with demonstrates like “Neighbors,” “Born to Bowl,” and “Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow” all on HBO Max. Industry observers note that not unlike its film slate, its series have been a blend of auteur-driven prestige and genre indicates with a twist. The David E. Kelley series “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” is a tongue-in-cheek, real-world satire on motherhood and the modern economy about a young single mom played by Elle Fanning who needs to turn to OnlyFans for extra cash. On the other side of the coin, “Crystal Lake” follows masked killer Jason Voorhees’ mom and stands out from other modern horror TV shows by, as our critic wrote, not trying to secretly be a family drama or a slapstick comedy or some other genre or metaphor, but it just amplifies the grisly kills in the best way it can.

The recurring theme between these highlights isn’t genre but the stamp of quality that A24 lends.

While something like “Beef” saw a steep drop in viewership of a reported 60 percent between its first and second seasons, “Euphoria” in its return was up 17 percent in its finale ratings compared to Season 2. “Crystal Lake” was also a major hit on Peacock, its top show on the streamer last month, logging 1.3 billion minutes watched over its first 11 days, making it the fourth-highest scripted original series ever on Peacock. A24 now has roughly 30 to 40 reveals in various stages of development, pre-production, or active production, with its executive team expanding from about 15 from just 3 people in its early days.

It’s been able to ramp up firstly because of its partnership with numerous TV buyers across the major streamers, but also because of working with largely first-time creators and showrunners. While “Crystal Lake” is a notable exception, A24 generally is operating on its TV side the same way it does with its film, leading with the artist and the project they want to pursue rather than the IP.

That has produced some very personal and idiosyncratic projects over the years like “Ramy” and “The Curse,” the latter of which was the kernel of getting Nathan Fielder to working with A24 again on “You Can See Everything.”.

It has been revealed that the breadth of content A24 has amassed on its TV side and continually making shows that have the same barrier-pushing flavor and stamp of quality that has become known with A24’s brand is what will help make it as essential a part of the tech giant’s overall business and valuation as its film and distribution business. But we’re seeing even its TV division branching out and embracing IP and tentpoles in the same way its film side has.

Coming up for A24 are a Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor drama “The Spot” on Hulu and “The Apology” with Gwyneth Paltrow on Netflix, which already got a two-season order and was an example of a show that grew out of Paltrow being convinced to try TV after already working with A24 on the film side for “Marty Supreme.” The studio is also is working with Ben Stiller on a Latest York Knicks documentary series for HBO and a competition cooking show based on the video game “Overcooked” for Netflix. A24 could’ve made a Knicks series with anyone, but teaming with a superfan like Stiller was another example of putting the creator above the concept.

It has been revealed that yet, both a strength and weakness of its TV model is that it does not have a distribution mechanism the way it does on the film side. It’s not bogged down with an unprofitable streamer, a dwindling linear cable channel, or a broadcast network, but that makes it reliant on the many partners it has built up across the industry.

Warner Bros. merging with Paramount arguably reduces the buyers in the market, even if there are still two streamers at Skydance. Netflix just had a massive shakeup of its leadership team that could easily have a different attitude toward A24’s series. And the overall industry trends around the end of Peak TV mean it’s always a volatile business for independents in the TV space.

But no one saw “Backrooms” or “You Can See Everything” coming either, and A24 has as good a chance as any to have lightning strike twice with the next “Euphoria” or “Beef.”.

According to recent reports, an official return to Gold and Silver’s Johto region has been officially confirmed for Pokémon Trading Card Game, with a new release set to arrive in 2027. The Pokémon Manufacturer International has already made a few announcements regarding what collections we’re getting in early 2027, but a new confirmation by Creatures has stirred the community, as we’re returning to Johto.

In a recent development, according to a new report by PokéBeach, Creatures, which is responsible for the TCG in Japan, has confirmed three new set releases for next year. Magma Heartbeat, Lightning Impact, and Aurora Ripples are three separate Pokémon TCG sets that will be released simultaneously on May 21, 2027, in Japan. Entei, Raikou, and Suicune are, respectively, the faces of these expansions. This is a major callback to the well-known Legendary Beasts of Generation 2’s Johto region. They had been teased earlier this year during Worlds in August, but have now been confirmed as the mascots for these new sets.

According to recent reports, unlike the first Pokémon TCG release of 2027, these three sets will be exclusive to Japan in May and will likely be fused into a single set for release in Western markets later on. This will be the first time that three sets are released simultaneously – usually, in Japan, dual sets are released together and are then combined into a single set for Western markets. One of the most key aspects of these three fresh sets is that they will kick off the Pokémon ex★ series for the TCG. How this new mechanic will work is still unclear.

It’s also unclear if the release of this Pokémon ex★ series will represent the end of the Mega Evolution ex series in the Card Game. If so, the release of Pokémon TCG: Flowing Fists in February may be one of the final ones from the Mega Evolution ex series, before the game transitions into the Pokémon ex★ series. On May 21, Creatures will also release six Battle Start Decks, all of which will also be part of the upcoming Pokémon ex★ series. The headliners for these decks are Decidueye, Blaziken, Dondozo, Dedenne, Alcremie, and Lucario.

The release of these upcoming sets and decks will coincide with the confirmed 2027 price increase for Pokémon TCG products. This, however, will happen exclusively in Japan. Booster packs will be 15% more expensive starting in May, so the new series will also officially represent the start of the price hike.

Sources indicate that the return to Gold and Silver’s Johto region with the three Legendary Beasts is exciting, even if it remains to be seen exactly how these sets will be adapted for the Western markets – it hasn’t been confirmed if the three sets will be fused into a single one, for example. Even so, for now, it’s the closest we’re getting to anything related to Gen 2. For now, we’ll have to be satisfied with this upcoming good-looking Pokémon Trading Card Game release.

Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone).
  • Most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it.
  • It has been revealed that now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my challenges, the upcoming device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it. They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo.The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

It has been revealed that now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that noted, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the new 10-inch model offers some substantial upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:.

Industry observers note that resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side.).

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

It's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than Aura's most popular offering, the 10.1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

I write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, November 17, the International Documentary Association (IDA) confirmed the nominees for its 42nd annual IDA Documentary Awards, including everything from the highly publicized blockbuster “You Can See Everything” to under-the-radar Best Documentary Feature contenders like “Concrete Land.”.

“I couldn’t be more excited to celebrate these meaningful and creative documentaries. It’s a challenging time for documentary makers, but also a really inspiring moment for IDA and for the field,” IDA Board President Ina Fichman remarked in a statement. “This year we see nominees whose deeply personal stories share narratives of resistance and exile, and we see artful, innovative filmmaking that is capturing fresh and robust audiences. I hope many will join us on December 4 as we honor our incredible community.” Related Stories A24’s TV Division Is Quietly Having as Strong a Year as Its Film Team ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Throws Netflix’s Oscar Campaign a Curveball.

The 2026 IDA Documentary Awards will also present the following special honors: the Career Achievement Award for the late Chilean filmmaker Patricio Guzmán; the Truth to Power Award for Amy Goodman and Juan González of Democracy Now!; the Emerging Filmmaker Award for Maia Lekow and Christopher King; and the Amicus Award for Cannes Docs, the documentary program of the Marché du Film led by Pierre-Alexis Chevit.

Industry observers note that this year, IDA received a record 650 entries in all categories from 95 countries, an increase over last year both in the total number of entries and the countries represented. 32 countries are represented among the final lineup of nominees.

IDA members from around the world will vote for the winners in the Best Feature Documentary and Best Short Documentary categories from November 17 to November 29, 2026. All other category winners are selected by juries representing the international documentary community.

The Awards will take place December 4, 2026, at The Ebell of Los Angeles, hosted for the second year in a row by documentary field leader Tabitha Jackson.

‘GTA 6’ Is Officially the Highest-Rated Game of All Time

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them.
  • Of all the games Rockstar Games had to beat this week, the one that gave it the most trouble came out on the Nintendo 64.
  • Grand Theft Auto 4 earned a 98 for Niko Bellic’s trip to Liberty City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Of all the games Rockstar Games had to beat this week, the one that gave it the most trouble came out on the Nintendo 64. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has held a 99 on Metacritic for years. Even Nintendo’s own remake fell three points short earlier this month, and its 96 was good enough to make it the best-reviewed game of 2026. Link got to enjoy that distinction for about two weeks.

Rockstar has come close before. Grand Theft Auto 4 earned a 98 for Niko Bellic’s trip to Liberty City. Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 both sit at 97, so that’s where the bar was when critics finally got to talk about Grand Theft Auto 6 on Wednesday morning, 13 years after Michael, Franklin, and Trevor first got together in Los Santos. It took more than a hundred reviews and a pair of car thieves to move it.

Sources indicate that the PS5 version of GTA 6 debuted at No. 1 on Metacritic’s Best Games of All Time list with a 99, matching the score of the original Ocarina of Time. Metacritic placed Rockstar’s game first despite the shared score, likely due to the higher number of reviews available. The score can still move as more reviews come in, but as of now, it seems unlikely to drop significantly.

In a recent development, jason and Lucia meet trying to steal the same car, which might be the most Grand Theft Auto way two people have ever fallen in love. ScreenRant’s Chris Carter gave the game a 10/10, writing that it “takes a page from Red Dead Redemption 2’s book.” That comparison makes more sense once you know what critics took away from the final missions. Over at The Guardian, Keza MacDonald described getting up and pacing in front of her TV because she was worried about what would happen to Jason and Lucia, which is a long way to come with a couple whose first shared interest is somebody else’s car.

Recent findings suggest that polygon’s Giovanni Colantonio found much of the fun in “a reactive place governed by intricate rules that beg to be bent and busted.” Take the question of what happens after you’ve successfully stolen a luxury car, for example. As NME’s Mark Beaumont discovered, cloning the key will get you into the driver’s seat, but the tracker still works, and it keeps telling the police where you are. Suddenly, there’s a pretty good argument for picking a cheaper car, which is the kind of decision Vice City used to leave to people who actually paid for them.

Game Rant’s Anthony Taormina also awarded GTA 6 a 10/10, calling Leonida “a world that is a joy to simply exist in.” For anyone who spent more time in GTA 5 driving around Los Santos with the radio on than they ever spent planning a heist, that might be the most persuasive line in any of the reviews.

Grand Theft Auto 6 launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Global stock markets have been under pressure as geopolitical tensions have resurfaced in the Middle East. Moreover, investors remain concerned about the sustainability of AI-driven demand and infrastructure spending.

In a recent development, nonetheless, those looking for attractive stock picks amid the ongoing volatility can gain key insights by tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. These experts assign ratings after in-depth analysis of a company's fundamentals, growth opportunities, and risks.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

E-commerce and cloud computing giant Amazon (AMZN) is this week's first pick. Heading into the company's second-quarter earnings, TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge reiterated a buy rating on AMZN stock, citing strength in the Amazon Web Services cloud unit as well as the e-commerce and advertising businesses. The analyst lowered his price target on AMZN stock to $340 from $350 as he revised his estimates and slightly raised his capex projections.

It has been revealed that specifically, Blackledge expects Amazon to report revenue of $200.1 billion, 2% above the Street's consensus, driven by acceleration in AWS and advertising revenue. He also expects the organization's e-commerce business to reflect the shifting of Prime Day in the U.S. and other key markets to the second quarter this year, compared with third quarter of last year.

In particular, Blackledge expects AWS revenue to grow 35.5% year-over-year in Q2 2026, marking an acceleration from 28.4% in the prior-year quarter and 3.4% above the Street's expectations. The 5-star analyst expects revenue to be driven by rising generative AI workloads as the tech giant's significant AI infrastructure spending helps to ease supply constraints.

Regarding third-quarter outlook, Blackledge said, "Our rev and Op Income estimates are 0.3% and 3.2% above consensus, driven by further AWS revenue growth acceleration led by AI demand.".

Blackledge ranks No. 771 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.2%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

It has been revealed that moving on to semiconductor organization Marvell Technology (MRVL). Following several meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a buy rating on MRVL stock with a price target of $360.

"Overall, the meetings reinforced our conviction that MRVL can sustain 40%+ growth for the next 3 years, driven by strong AI demand, optical connectivity leadership, and expanding Custom pipeline," said Pajjuri.

It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst added that robust demand and limited supply are giving greater revenue visibility. Pajjuri noted that Marvell's data center business is on track to deliver more than 50% growth this year and next. Also, the growth in the company's networking business is outpacing compute, driven by agentic AI and inferencing workloads.

Meanwhile, Pajjuri noted that optical product lead times have extended to more than six months, while XPU customers are placing purchase orders 12 months in advance. While the analyst kept his estimates unchanged, he sees the possibility of upside for the second half of 2026 from the Optical business, with more significant upside potential for 2027 and 2028 estimates.

According to recent reports, furthermore, Pajjuri noted that Marvell's scale-across offering is emerging as an additional growth catalyst for 2027, while scale-up networking is expected to present a multibillion-dollar greenfield serviceable addressable market. Also, management is upbeat about Marvell's custom business, with the company targeting more than $10 billion in revenue for 2028, driven by existing programs with Amazon's AWS and Microsoft and multiple XPU attach wins.

Pajjuri ranks No. 88 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 51.5%. See Marvell Options Activity on TipRanks.

Recent findings suggest that chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is scheduled to announce its second-quarter earnings on Aug. 4. Shares have seen a strong jump year-to-date due to demand for the company's AI GPUs and server CPUs.

Ahead of second-quarter earnings, Wells Fargo analyst Aaron Rakers reaffirmed a buy rating on AMD stock and raised his price target to $615 from $505, citing "increasing focus on path to +$20/sh. EPS in CY28." The analyst expects AMD to reiterate its confidence in the MI450 series and Helios ramp beginning in the third quarter of 2026.

The 5-star analyst increased his estimates for AMD server CPU revenue to $16.0 billion (up 68% year-over-year), $20.5 billion (up 28%), and $25.0 billion (up 22%) for 2026, 2027, 2028, respectively. Rakers noted that in the previous quarter, AMD increased its server CPU total addressable market estimates to $120 billion by 2030, representing a more than 35% compound annual growth rate.

Sources indicate that rakers expects AMD to comment on an additional rise in server CPU demand since its first-quarter results. He sees upside driven by agentic AI demand momentum, cloud demand, and traditional enterprise modernization. In this regard, the analyst highlighted that Micron increased its 2026 server shipment guidance recently. Also, checks indicate continued upside to the average selling price.

Meanwhile, Rakers' data center GPU estimates remain above consensus at $15.6 billion, $40.6 billion, and $63.0 billion for 2026, 2027, and 2028, respectively, while estimates for the client and gaming businesses are below the Street's consensus. Overall, the analyst projects EPS of $7.15, $13.40, and $18.75 for 2026, 2027, and 2028, respectively.

GTA 6: How To Change Your Clothes & Save Outfits

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in GTA 6, style can be extremely crucial.
  • According to recent reports, as an open-world game with a dense world, fans will immediately flock to the customization system, which runs very deep in GTA 6.
  • According to recent reports, changing clothes is unlocked shortly after you start the main game (following the chase with Brian, and meeting one of his associates at a pool party), when you only control Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in GTA 6, style can be extremely crucial. While it's not paramount to gameplay, it can affect how the authorities recognize you; plus, Jason and Lucia constantly change gear to suit any given mission. For some players, the cosmetic aspect of any open-world game is the game itself.

According to recent reports, as an open-world game with a dense world, fans will immediately flock to the customization system, which runs very deep in GTA 6. Here's how to find new outfits, change into them, and keep a supply of clothes on hand for when things really go south out in the wild. More so than ever, clothes have a pretty important role in the game.

According to recent reports, changing clothes is unlocked shortly after you start the main game (following the chase with Brian, and meeting one of his associates at a pool party), when you only control Jason. Once you acquire Lucia, and she joins the fray as a main character, you'll be able to alter her style as well.

Changing your clothes in GTA 6 is primarily done in two ways:.

According to recent reports, stores are marked with a black T-shirt icon and sell clothes, but many other locations can provide outfits as well, like gun shops, which sell camo/tactical gear and the like. In other words, your options are vast, and once you start traveling past the original Chapter 1 Florida Keys location, you'll find more stores than you can handle.

Alternatively, you can visit a barber to change up Jason's facial hair, hair color, and style (the same goes for Lucia's hairstyle when she's available). Using all of these tools, you can utterly alter how Jason and Lucia look compared to their "canon/trailer" character models.

It has been revealed that once you're comfortable with an outfit, go to the outfit menu in the dresser interface, then press and hold Square on PlayStation (X on Xbox) to add it to the trunk. You can have five outfits saved in the trunk,.

It's vital to note that this needs to be a registered car. Initially, you're given access to Jason's car, which can be recovered no matter what using towing services, even if it drives off a cliff and explodes. That way, your outfits will always be safe and can't be destroyed because of a mission-based mishap.

It has been revealed that outfits stored away in your trunk can be extremely useful, as police scan for how the suspects were dressed at the time of the crime. So if you were wearing an orange jumpsuit for a robbery, and successfully escape, you can change outfits (and potentially vehicles) to make a clean getaway. Try to have at least two outfits stored away for this express purpose.

According to recent reports, with all the customization options available in GTA 6, odds are you're going to be using the outfit system quite a bit. Just be sure to change your look periodically on the go to avoid police detection.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that though the days when every film gets a massive DVD release are gone, and all kinds of logistics shape how companies like GKIDS proposal home releases, the core requirement remains the same. Someone on the GKIDS team has to be a fan.

According to recent reports, director of Home Entertainment Alison Kozberg is a fan of all the titles the company is releasing this winter, from the incredibly personal and warm “Linda Linda Linda” to the more wrenching (though you would expect nothing less from Hideaki Anno) “Love & Pop.” But crafting a personal fan experience dictates the presentation and bonus features behind each release, and that can look wildly different for each title GKIDS puts out. Related Stories IDA Documentary Awards 2026 Nominations: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Concrete Land,’ and More Earn Nods ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Throws Netflix’s Oscar Campaign a Curveball.

According to recent reports, “ Every project is really different. Every project has different access. Some films have creators that are living; some films don’t. Some films have a rich archive; others don’t. So you’re always navigating different conditions of production,” Kozberg told IndieWire. “[We think about] what is emotionally resonant for us. And we really have conversations about that. What do we feel about this film? What artwork and images impact us? What is particularly interesting? Like, when thinking about bonus features, you also think about what captures your imagination.”.

Sources indicate that when it came to putting out a box set for the Netflix series “Arcane,” for instance, the team was guided by the incredibly rich tradition of cosplay and fanworks in the “League of Legends” community online. They imagined fun art that would be right at home in an artists’ alley at a convention expo hall, and that guided everything from the art on the discs to the set of dice that came in the box set. But with this year’s collector’s edition of “Angel’s Egg,” the incredible collaboration between director Mamoru Oshii (“Ghost in the Shell”) and legendary artist Yoshitaka Amano, the home entertainment team wanted to cultivate a completely different experience.

Recent findings suggest that “We were really, really, really passionate about being able to bring ‘Angel’s Egg’ to people in North America, both theatrically and on disc,” Kozberg said. “We really, really wanted to create a forum to extend access to the creators, but also to create access to Amano’s artwork, which we know fans are so passionate about, and which is so exquisite. So when putting the package together, we tried to be really thoughtful, and really restrained, and really platform these beautiful illustrations.”.

In a recent development, it was also important for the set to do what great home releases have been doing since we all went hunting for behind-the-scenes content hidden as Easter Eggs inside DVD menus. It was important to teach curious audiences about how filmmaking works and the context that makes a particular story such a miracle to have gotten made. The interviews and essay booklet were designed to build the historical context for a film as dense and thematically rich as “Angel’s Egg” and to give fans a platform to extend their conversations about it.

“We’re always thinking about ways to additionally kind of facilitate and support other people’s creative inspiration,” Kozberg mentioned. “And  there is a real genuine joy to having objects connected to films you love in your life. I look at the ‘Angel’s Egg’ art cards. I think it feels really special and joyful to be able to have those displayed in your home, to think about ‘Angel’s Egg’ in the day-to-day, to see the artwork.”.

Industry observers note that while GKIDS releases a mix of live-action and animated titles, the overall theme of their work is facilitating fandom. “We talk a lot about kind of like seeing people’s fandom and reflecting it back to them. So [our goal] is understanding what about a film is emotionally resonant, and then creating opportunities to reflect and engage with that emotion,” Kozberg said.

#27843. 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Sources indicate that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Sources indicate that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

According to recent reports, no matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar notes that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

In a recent development, while PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

In the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar claims that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the firm hasn't explained why that is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has a lot going on, and it's really easy to miss things. For instance, after you start your journey, you'll take control of Jason, who is trying to make the Florida Keys feel like home while waiting for his partner, Lucia, to get out of Leonida Penitentiary.

In a recent development, in the process, all sorts of errands open up, including shopping for fresh clothes and groceries, as well as fixing up the initial house the game provides as a home base. While it's not required to do housework in GTA 6, there is a benefit.

It has been revealed that you might be wondering: "Why even bother fixing up Jason's house?" Well, the jobs don't take as long as you'd think (they start as realistic handiwork, then shift into a montage, and finish up in a few minutes), plus they can add extra relationship points for Jason and Lucia. Fixing everything up will allow Jason and Lucia to get off on the right foot.

Industry observers note that when you start the game and wander over to Jason's house as part of the story, you'll notice it's in disrepair. Jason will fix the roof a bit, but you can visit later to fully repair it and eliminate the leak.

According to recent reports, this is one of the easiest spots to find since you'll just need to climb up a ladder near the front door (the front exit is near the bathroom). Do it early, before you forget.

According to recent reports, the outdoor ground stairwell that leads up to the house is another spot that's easy to miss. Walk over to the stairwell closest to the mailbox and interact with it to fix it, grab newly introduced boards, and nail them in.

Lucia will be thankful when she returns from jail; it's one of the first things she'll notice about the house, and all the work Jason has done while off on his own.

The other bit you'll need to fix is at the top of the same stairwell outdoors. Before you go up another flight of small stairs into the house, check out the deck fence; it needs repairing.

In a recent development, before you can really transform the room into something special, you'll need to put up drywall in your bedroom. Head over to your master bedroom (next to the wardrobe, connected to the main living room) and interact with the wall. You'll nail in some drywall and create a real living space.

After that, you can paint the room and complete your house transformation. You're almost there, and since the entire process takes around 15 minutes total, it's a small ask.

According to recent reports, one of your last steps to painting the bedroom. Jason will grab a roller and start rolling, eventually transforming the entire bedroom into a nice little area. With all the repairs complete, the game gives you a quick congrats with an in-game message, and your heart meter rises.

This allows Lucia to be in good spirits after coming home. In fact, she was "crazy in love" with Jason, the third tier (of four) on the relationship meter. Doing this small task will help you make up for some relationship mistakes you'll eventually make in GTA 6.
