In a recent development, just when you thought this year couldn't get any better for Robert Pattinson, he has been officially declared as the new James Bond. Following in the footsteps of Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, and Daniel Craig, Pattinson will help lead cinema's greatest spy series into a bold new era under Amazon, after its billion-dollar acquisition of the franchise. Pattinson will re-team with Dune: Part Three director Denis Villeneuve on the next movie, with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight penning the script.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson mentioned in a statement as the first days of a upcoming era begin. This new role for the man who is also Matt Reeves' The Batman feels like a reward for his faultless year of film, which includes stand-out performances in Christopher Nolan's epic adaptation of The Odyssey, A24's The Drama alongside Zendaya, and the aforementioned Dune: Part Three, which is heading to theaters on December 18.

It has been revealed that but not only has Pattinson become the next Bond, but he might even become an Academy Award winner next year for his hugely impressive lead performance in Lance Oppenheim's Primetime, another A24 movie from this year. Based on the television series To Catch a Predator, with Pattinson portraying Chris Hansen, Primetime took a hugely controversial subject and managed to mold it into one of the best-reviewed films of the year, thanks in no small part to the lead performance of our new 007. Collider's Taylor Gates called Pattinson's performance his best in her review, "not just of this year, but of his entire career.".

No doubt boosted by the newly introduced Bond announcement, Primetime has now jumped up the streaming charts, officially ranking as the sixth-most-watched movie on the Apple TV Store in the U.S. The current top spot on the platform is held by David Ayer and Brad Pitt's new survival thriller, Heart of the Beast, which scored just shy of $200 million at the box office before moving to PVOD. Primetime made $57.8 million during its theatrical run against a $15 million budget.

For all the latest streaming stories, make sure to stay tuned to Collider.

In this episode, we're talking televisions.

In a recent development, I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

Recent findings suggest that I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how big the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

Sources indicate that these glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

Recent findings suggest that then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a substantial screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

It has been revealed that they plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

According to recent reports, “Tapping into the increasingly resonant themes of social pressure, groupthink and the universal desire to belong, Games We Play follows Imogen (Pitts), who joins her boyfriend Jack (Cott) and his two childhood best friends, Gage (McTee) and Freddie (Faison), for a weekend getaway. When she finds herself the unmistakable outsider, Imogen becomes desperate to win their approval. But as she is forced to participate in a tournament of high-stakes games, the experience takes a sinister turn, pushing her to compromise her identity and instincts while questioning both her sanity and her safety. What begins as a pursuit of acceptance spirals into a chilling psychological game where the stakes are far more dangerous than fitting in.”.

Vertical, which holds North American rights, will release Games We Play in select theaters and on VOD on December 4. Blue Fox Entertainment has acquired the film’s international rights and is introducing it to buyers at the American Film Market.

Recent findings suggest that the trailer finds Imogen playing along with Jack’s friends, joining a round of Sardines and surrendering her phone for their tournament in an effort to become part of the group. Things soon take a darker turn as Gage’s interest in Imogen becomes a little too intense, and rather than questioning his friends’ behavior, Jack starts questioning her. The result looks twisted and genuinely unsettling, turning the kinds of games that felt harmless as kids into something far more menacing.

According to recent reports, games We Play appears to borrow the same scare tactic that made Ready or Not work so well: take a game everyone knows how to play and raise the stakes until it becomes a fight for survival. Because the rules are so familiar, it’s easy for viewers to put themselves in Imogen’s shoes. She goes along with everything for her boyfriend’s sake, and who hasn’t wanted to win over a fresh group of friends? It’s a relatable impulse, just not one worth following once the games start turning deadly.

“Games We Play is a timely examination of the universal struggle for social survival, where the desire to belong can become just as dangerous as the fight to stay alive,” said Scharlin Ben-Hamoo, who also serves as an executive producer alongside Pitts.

“Rachael Dahl has crafted a compelling psychological thriller that taps into the pressures we all recognize, while taking them to a terrifying extreme. We are excited to partner with Vertical Entertainment and Blue Fox Entertainment to bring this story to audiences around the world.”.

It has been revealed that produced by Taryn Gates and Raza Rizvi (Lemonade Blessing), Games We Play arrives in select theaters and on VOD on December 4. Check out the exclusive trailer above.

Tech Report: 10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it.
  • Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address.
  • If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a upcoming service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

Industry observers note that google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

Recent findings suggest that timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

You can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

While Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the company does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

According to recent reports, A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

According to recent reports, if you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

Google uses data from Gmail and Google Drive to target ads, which means that your emails, files, and photos could be used for monetization. To stop this, you'll need to disable Personal Intelligence. To turn it off, visit this settings page, and click Turn off Personal Intelligence.

Latest Update: Garmin Cyclists Can Now Make Themselves Appear on Waze in Real Time

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • Sources indicate that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a latest layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • Sources indicate that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

Sources indicate that for riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a latest layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Sources indicate that riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze owners near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

The feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin notes this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

Recent findings suggest that garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This fresh feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

It has been revealed that this feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more users, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

Sources indicate that it depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

In a recent development, finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

GTA 6: How To Easily Fast Travel

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you're making an open-world game, odds are it has a fast travel mechanic.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 is modeled after Miami after all, so it would make sense to add in some slower, more relaxing options.
  • Recent findings suggest that depending on where you are in the game, you can call a taxi or an Uber; they are functionally the same.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you're making an open-world game, odds are it has a fast travel mechanic. As projects have gotten bigger and bigger, it's become a necessity, as not everyone has the time to walk across the world at any given moment. Thankfully, GTA 6 is here to answer the call, but it also offers a few other options for folks looking for a more relaxed open-world experience.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is modeled after Miami after all, so it would make sense to add in some slower, more relaxing options. Here's how to unlock fast travel, and if you want, also use a form of "slow travel" to get through Vice City and the surrounding county.

Recent findings suggest that depending on where you are in the game, you can call a taxi or an Uber; they are functionally the same. At the start of GTA 6, you'll need to call "Paradise Taxi" from your contacts (the green phone icon) on your phone interface. All you have to do is press up on the direction pad to bring up your phone (which can be done in a vehicle while driving as well), select contacts, then Paradise Taxi.

The taxi will then drive over to your location in less than 10 seconds. Sometimes it'll drift off to the side due to a pathing issue (sometimes traffic can be a factor), so you may need to look for a little white taxi/vehicle icon on your minimap and walk over to it. Note that you cannot call a taxi if you're in a completely isolated area, like an island off the Florida Keys, or a swampy zone where vehicles can't easily traverse.

Later in the game, you'll acquire an Uber-like app to call for a ride. This is a bit more involved, as you can set your destination either before opening the app or after, and change your destination more easily.

You might notice that when entering the vehicle, it's not set to "fast travel" right away. The driver will generally greet you (or say some eccentric dialogue), then you'll confirm the destination and head out in real time. Your driver will then let you take in the sights of Vice City and the surrounding area as you head to your destination.

Industry observers note that if you want to get there a little quicker, you can tell them to "hurry up" for a small fee. Open the NPC menu by holding L2 (something you can do in pretty much every store or near any service in the game), and tell them to hurry. Or, if you're in the mood for actual fast travel, you can skip the ride for $100 in-game cash.

You can set up your destination ahead of time on your map screen by selecting a point of interest, then call the taxi/Uber.

It has been revealed that this process of skipping travel is very expensive early on, when you're scrimping and saving just a few thousand dollars. But later in the game, it's something you can pay for every time if you want to get places rapidly. Any GTA 6 fan knows the world map is gigantic for any given release, so it's crucial to cover a lot of ground when you need to.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Palestinian-Syrian filmmaker Abdallah Al-Khatib’s award-winning drama Chronicles from the Siege has been pulled by its producers from Morocco’s Marrakech International Film Festival on the eve of its opening.

The drama, about Palestinian civilians trapped in a war zone, was to have played in the festival’s main competition aimed at first and second features and featuring a jury presided over by Marion Cotillard this year.

Recent findings suggest that “The Marrakech International Film Festival has been informed of the decision by Algerian production company Issaad Film Productions, the rights holder of Chronicles from The Siege… to withdraw the film from the Official Competition of the Festival’s 23rd edition,” Marrakech stated in a statement. Related Stories Documentary Watermelon Pictures Condemns Killing Of 'American Doctor' Surgeon In Gaza Hospital Strike News 'NAZA' Becomes One Of The Most Watched Docs On Theatrical Release In 2026.

The festival said the producers had originally confirmed the participation of Chronicles from the Siege, on June 1, and that Al-Khatib was not in agreement with the move to withdraw the film. Watch on Deadline.

“Abdallah Al-Khatib has strongly opposed this decision, both to the film’s producers and to the festival, and has made clear his wish for the film to remain in the Official Competition and be presented in Marrakech,” read the statement.

“While the Festival acknowledges the director’s expressed wish to present his film in Marrakech, it is bound to respect the decision of the organization holding the film’s rights and is therefore unable to retain it in the Festival’s programme,” continued the statement.

In a recent development, deadline has contacted Issaad Film Productions to clarify why it pulled film and is waiting for a response. There are long-simmering tensions between North African neighbors Algeria and Morocco, but this does not seem to have prompted the withdrawal.

Deadline understands that the producers have instead cited the recent upgrading of diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israeli, which was unveiled in September.

Prior to its selection for Marrakech’s Competition, the film was supported by the festival’s Atlas Workshops project incubator, attending its 2024 edition where it was awarded the Atlas Prize for Post-Production.

Chronicles from the Siege world premiered in February in the Berlinale in Germany, which also has diplomatic relations with Israel.

It went on to win the Best First Feature Award in a politically-charged awards ceremony in which Al-Khatib, accused the German government of “complicity” in Israel’s oppression of Palestinians, prompting a minister in the room to walk out.

This speech, alongside a number of public condemnations of Israel’s actions in Gaza by other winners, triggered a conservative and far-right political backlash against the festival and calls for Berlinale director Tricia Tuttle to be removed from her job.

The festival said the speeches had been within the realms of free speech and an international campaign of solidarity from across the film world helped keep Tuttle in her role.

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: massive sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • According to recent reports, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: massive sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and significant ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the newly introduced crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things promptly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things promptly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

In a recent development, adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

The story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them.
  • Matt Damon has had a rough time getting home in Christopher Nolan’s movies.
  • In a recent development, audiences followed him to the tune of $1.8 billion worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

Matt Damon has had a rough time getting home in Christopher Nolan’s movies. In Interstellar, somebody finally comes to collect him, and he immediately makes everybody regret it. The Odyssey gives him a much better reason to want the trip to end. As Odysseus, he has a wife and son waiting in Ithaca, with the aftermath of the Trojan War and a succession of gods and monsters between them. Nolan shot the journey around the world, making the sea itself one of the problems his cast and crew had to contend with.

In a recent development, audiences followed him to the tune of $1.8 billion worldwide. According to NBCUniversal, that makes The Odyssey the biggest movie of Nolan’s career and the highest-grossing release in Universal Pictures’ history. The first movie shot entirely in IMAX has spent months giving people a reason to find the biggest screen within driving distance. Now the people who have already made that trip can finally spend some time looking at how Nolan pulled it off.

The Odyssey is available to watch at home as of November 17. The movie is available to buy or rent through digital retailers including Prime Video, the Apple TV app, and Fandango at Home, with 4K Ultra HD, Blu-ray, and DVD editions arriving the same day. Damon leads a cast that includes Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Zendaya, Samantha Morton, and Charlize Theron.

Industry observers note that four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

In a recent development, you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

The home release includes more than 90 minutes of special features, with a collection of 12 production featurettes personally overseen by Nolan. The Trojan Horse gets a feature of its own, which feels fair for a prop that has to fool an entire city while the audience already knows what’s inside. Other pieces follow the construction of Troy in Morocco, the ships used for the voyage, and the stunt work with Damon and Holland.

Recent findings suggest that the physical editions also include the IMAX prologue, along with a conversation in which Reece Feldman asks Nolan to explain what happens to the movie after it leaves the set. Ludwig Göransson takes viewers through the score in a separate featurette, including the instruments and vocals used to build it. Together, the extras give the production’s enormous scale some individual faces. Somebody had to make those ships seaworthy, dress those armies, and get the cameras into position before Odysseus could have the worst trip of his life.

The Odyssey is available now on digital and physical formats.

GTA 6: How To Easily Find Story Missions

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 is a stunningly deep open-world game with a lot to do, but naturally, the story mode is what a lot of players will gravitate toward.
  • Here's how to always stay on top of what missions you need to advance the story, and how to move things along if they need a little nudge.
  • Press the touchpad on PS5 to open the map, which brings up a variety of missions and points of interest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is a stunningly deep open-world game with a lot to do, but naturally, the story mode is what a lot of players will gravitate toward. While many of the transitions to these missions are going to be natural, in classic GTA fashion, there are a handful of missions that aren't so obvious, and require a degree of waiting or a proactive approach.

Here's how to always stay on top of what missions you need to advance the story, and how to move things along if they need a little nudge. Given the direct control you have over both Jason and Lucia as protagonists, it's important to know all the tricks so you don't get stuck.

Press the touchpad on PS5 to open the map, which brings up a variety of missions and points of interest. Think of your map as a master list of everything to do, with icons for drop points (to stash/sell illicit objects), side quests, shops, banks to rob, and, of course, story missions.

Industry observers note that these are indicated by a "book" icon near the top left of the screen, listing all story missions you can take part in. For the most part, this list will include at least one mission, all of which are required to progress "Jason and Lucia's Story," the campaign of GTA 6.

Note that occasionally, Lucia or Jason will be forced to go on solo missions. Think Lucia meeting up with her mom for a mother-daughter day, or Jason doing an odd job for an old friend that Lucia isn't interested in attending.

In a recent development, when these missions arise, make sure you say goodbye to your partner before entering the mission area. Sometimes the mission won't progress unless the required character's significant other is completely out of the zone, so if you're having trouble starting a story mission, that might be why.

We recommend knocking these story missions out as soon as possible, as they can be finicky and block progress on other missions.

When story missions aren't listed, here are the two things you can do to speed things up:.

The game doesn't make it immediately apparent, but sometimes calling a key character is enough to advance the story. As you call each contact in the recents menu, they will disappear, indicating you have all the info you need from them, and a story mission may populate as soon as the call ends. By going to bed afterward, you can accelerate this story mission prep process and move things along.

It has been revealed that if you're looking to go through the story of GTA 6 at a brisker pace, we recommend doing both in tandem. Go to bed at your home location, sleep until the next day, then call as many people as you can. It might take a few days, but story missions will pop up over time.

#27822. The Apple Watch's Upcoming 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

The Apple Watch's Upcoming 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1353 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that debuted at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

In a recent development, music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this released in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

It has been revealed that live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just noted in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

According to recent reports, but Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

As promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was said. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

It has been revealed that but still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people mentioned to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

In a recent development, but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

It has been revealed that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most notable points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tudor Vladimir Panduru touched down at the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival in Poland last week where the cinematographer and frequent Cristian Mungiu collaborator reflected on how he crafted the visuals for the Romanian filmmaker’s Palme d’Or winning title Fjord.

Sources indicate that panduru and Mungiu have been working together for more than a decade, working on titles such as Graduation and R.M.N. in addition to Fjord, and the DP notes that the long relationship means they have built a shorthand and “very specific visual language” together.

Mungiu is known for his very long takes – notably shooting a 17-minute shot in R.M.N. – and Panduru states the pair have “perfected the way we work with these long takes.” Related Stories Festivals 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' DP On Balancing Action Sequences With A Man's "Spiritual Journey And Struggles Of Trying To Step Up As A Father" -- ToruńCamerimage Festivals 'Fatherland' Takes Top Prize At ToruńCamerimage; 'Wild Horse Nine' Wins Audience Award.

It has been revealed that “We are comfortable with each other and we prepare a lot,” he says. “He brought me in on this project quite early on in pre-production and then we went to Norway to scout for locations.” Watch on Deadline.

Fjord, which is released by Neon in the U.S. and UK, follows a Norwegian woman (Renate Reinsve) and her devout Romanian husband (Sebastian Stan) who relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgement that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

“Cristian is a good observer, and he always wants to be truthful,” indicates Panduru. “And I follow that in that process of trying not to be judgemental in my approach as well.

He continues: “From the point of the script, the story had some specificity. The fact that these two families were close to each other meant that we had to find a place or a geography that would tell that from the start, and that was the hardest thing throughout the process of the scout.”.

According to recent reports, the team scouted from Bergen to Ålesund before finding neighbouring houses overlooking the water for the main characters. “It wasn’t so common to find two houses in such close vicinity because when we took the first photos and watched them, we were totally immersed in that universe. So, that’s a layer that wasn’t present in the script.”.

Industry observers note that he admits that scheduling and the remote location made it a “hard production” at times. “It was tricky organizing everything and getting to the locations. You had to either take two ferries or a long road and a ferry, so we were quite stuck there. It was really remote.”.

A further challenge, he notes, was the fact that the story takes place across three seasons but was only shot in March and April. “When we scouted the third time in January, there was a lot of snow and we were hoping to have images with small characters in the snow, but it wasn’t like that. We had to use a bit of VFX on the way. The only evening shots that had a lot of snow were shot on the weekend because that’s when it happened.

“Our first AD was the one who proposed we shoot when it was snowing at the weekend and we even convinced Sebastian to come with us for one of the shots. I think that was a really interesting part of doing Fjord, was the fact that the crew, who were from Romania, Norway, Finland, Sweden and all over, was really homogenous. We really were like a family, so we felt support from all sides.”.

Thanks to weather conditions, Panduru points out that one of the film’s more emotional scenes when Reinsve’s character’s children are taken into custody, was actually shot on the first day of the shoot “because we were supposed to shoot in the snow.”.

“Shooting such an intense scene for the first day was really interesting but, in a way, because we did that at the beginning, everybody understood what the film was about,” he states.

Panduru says that one of the most challenging sequences was the “jump in the water”, a long take which sees the camera follow Reinsve’s character searching on the ground to jumping into the sea.

According to recent reports, “Because we shoot in these long takes, the most important thing was to have the emotional trajectory of the situation,” he claims. “We thought a lot about how to achieve that moment in a technical way, and we thought about cranes and drones, but it wasn’t the right thing. I proposed to Cristian to test to see if I could physically jump in the water with them and we did it in a weekend and it worked.”.

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (846 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

In a recent development, many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in upcoming Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Industry observers note that if you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Recent findings suggest that reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Recent findings suggest that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

In a recent development, in this scenario, investors seeking steady income can consider adding dividend stocks to their portfolios. Recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help them pick attractive dividend stocks that are backed by solid cash flows to support consistent payments.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

It has been revealed that oil and gas exploration and production tech giant ConocoPhillips is this week's first dividend pick. It has been revealed that ahead of second-quarter results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin reiterated a buy rating on COP stock with a price target of $183. Despite the pressure on oil prices from an increase in OPEC production quota, the analyst finds ConocoPhillips and Shell stocks appealing as the earnings season approaches. He cited their operational visibility and resilience as factors backing their appeal.

Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst expects ConocoPhillips to meet its production guidance of 2.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day at the mid-point. He expects lower Waha natural gas prices in the Permian Basin to be offset by stronger Brent crude premiums. Margolin expects capital expenditure to remain within COP's prior guided range of $12.2 billion annualized, with no significant impact on spending on the Northfield East project in Qatar despite the Strait of Hormuz disruption.

In a recent development, overall, Margolin expects COP to generate about $3.5 billion in free cash flow (before working capital) and earnings per share of $2.94. He expects continued strength in COP's free cash flow and regular dividend growth through the completion of the Willow project in 2028/2029. Prior to the Willow project coming online, the analyst expects free cash flow to grow by about $2 billion in 2027 and 2028, assuming Brent crude averages around $60 per barrel.

"COP's track record of capital efficiency and strong Permian well productivity underpins its ability to pursue long-cycle developments," remarked Margolin.

In a recent development, margolin ranks No. 457 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 70% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.3%. See ConocoPhillips Financials on TipRanks.

Energy Transfer is a limited partnership that operates 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. With a quarterly cash distribution of 33.75 cents per common unit ($1.35 per unit on an annualized basis), ET offers a yield of 6.8%.

Heading into Energy Transfer's Q2 earnings on Aug. 4, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith reaffirmed a buy rating on ET stock with a price target of $23. The analyst noted that his adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization estimate of $4.46 billion is 1% below the Street's consensus of $4.49 billion.

The 5-star analyst noted that Energy Transfer has slightly outperformed Enterprise Products Partners recently. However, it still trades at a relative discount of 19% compared to EPD, which is below its historical discount range of 17%-20%. Smith believes that ET stock could be re-rated higher if the organization provides a clearer long-term strategy for natural gas growth.

Industry observers note that furthermore, Smith expects the current energy market to support a stronger outlook for natural gas liquids and crude oil. "The current energy macro backdrop positions ET to benefit in all three commodities," stated the analyst.

He expects Energy Transfer's adjusted EBITDA to grow at a 4.8% compound annual growth rate in 2027-2030, which is 1%-3% above Wall Street's expectations. In fact, Smith sees the possibility of additional upside if ET introduces more natural gas projects. He added that investors will await details on final investment decisions on fresh natural gas projects and any clues about additional projects in the pipeline. The analyst noted that ET has unveiled new gas projects consistently in recent quarters.

Smith ranks No. 550 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.4%. See Energy Transfer Statistics on TipRanks.

It has been revealed that finally, let's look at energy giant Chevron, which is scheduled to announce its second-quarter results on July 31. Last month, the firm paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12, CVX offers a dividend yield of 3.92%.

Ahead of Q2 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on Chevron stock and lowered his price target to $216 from $236. Byrne expects the organization to report adjusted EPS of about $5.86 per share, nearly 9% above the Street's expectations.

Additionally, the analyst expects Chevron to generate $18.2 billion in cash flow from operations (before working capital changes), driven by stronger earnings and about $2.2 billion in dividends from affiliated companies. Unlike the first quarter, Chevron is not expected to make a TCO loan repayment in Q2, providing an additional boost to cash flow.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (829 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations.
  • Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows.
  • It has been revealed that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

It has been revealed that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

In a recent development, if you have a long list of demonstrates and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

Sources indicate that if you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Sources indicate that hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download highlights and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

If you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can upgrade your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

DEADLINE: What was the feedback after the first edition of the Industry days?

Industry observers note that HASSAN AL-THAWADI: The feedback around Industry Days was very encouraging. The first edition gave us an opportunity to introduce our vision for Qatar’s film industry, engage the region and hear directly from filmmakers, studios, producers and financiers.

More importantly, after the event, we understood that our vision resonated with support for the ecosystem around financing, production, talent, infrastructure and access to the region we are trying to build.

This edition is about sharing what has moved forward and the progress we have made over the past year, what we have learned, how we have adapted, and what comes next.

Industry observers note that AL-THAWADI: There will be some new announcements, but I will leave the specifics for Doha. Recent findings suggest that AL-THAWADI: We can’t escape the difficult period our region has experienced. However, the fundamentals of what we are trying to build has not changed. We have a long-term strategy to attract international production, develop Arab talent and capability and to create a stronger platform for stories from our region to reach global audiences.

DEADLINE: Are companies still interested in setting up here or striking partnerships?

Sources indicate that AL-THAWADI: Absolutely. We continue to see strong interest, although I think the nature of the conversation has matured. A year ago, much of the discussion was about the proposition of Qatar.

Sources indicate that today, the conversations are increasingly around specific projects, production activity, financing, services and access to the wider region. We are already seeing that translate into production activity through the Qatar Screen Production Incentive, alongside continued engagement with international studios and production partners.

Recent findings suggest that the objective is not simply to have companies establish a presence in Qatar. For us, what matters most is sustained activity: productions being made, capability being transferred, local and regional talent being developed, and commercial relationships that give companies a reason to continue investing and working here and across the region. That is what we are building, and we continue to see appetite for it.

DEADLINE: Have any productions accessed the rebate?

Industry observers note that AL-THAWADI: Yes. We have pilot productions already leveraging the Qatar Screen Production Incentive. For us, the crucial point is that we are beginning to see the incentive translate into real production activity, jobs and opportunities within Qatar, and now we’re extending its reach. We are strengthening regional collaboration and building the infrastructure that is required for global studios to film and produce in countries across the region.

AL-THAWADI: We are still in discussions with our production partner, Eon, and look forward to sharing further developments once confirmed.

DEADLINE: What’s your long-term view for Qatar’s future as a media and entertainment hub?

We believe Qatar can become both a gateway and a platform that serves as regional hub for the global film and entertainment industry: a gateway connecting talent, creatives and companies from our region to global markets, and a platform where international partners can work with the talent, stories and capabilities of the Arab world.

My long-term view for Qatar as a hub for the global film and entertainment industry continues to be ambitious, expansive and collaborative. Success for us is not simply how many productions shoot in Qatar. It is whether we build a sustainable ecosystem with the necessary financing, production, post-production, distribution, talent development, technology and infrastructure to create lasting cultural and economic value in Qatar and across the region.

It has been revealed that arab storytelling remains underrepresented globally. Our goal is to help create the conditions for those stories to be developed at the highest level and reach audiences around the world, while at the same time making Qatar a serious and trusted destination for international production.

One of the lessons of the World Cup is that when you invest with a clear long-term purpose, you can build capability and create a legacy that extends far beyond the event itself. Film has that same ability to bring people together and broaden representation. We are still at the beginning of that journey, but the direction is very clear.
